木槽鼓屬體鳴樂器，發聲時整體振動，不以鼓皮振動為主要聲源。其共鳴腔由樹幹或竹材鑿: The log drum is an idiophone: the whole body vibrates, and a drumhead is not the main source of sound. Its resonating chamber is hollowed from a tree trunk or a length of bamboo, and when the edge of the slit or a tongue is struck, the chamber amplifies the sound and it comes out through the opening. Differences in pitch come from the area and thickness of the tongues; a single slit, two slits or three slits can give different pitches, and if the volume of the chamber matches the intended pitch the instrument speaks more efficiently and more loudly. Compared with a true drum, which has a head, it sounds through the vibration of the chamber and the tongues, and it is used for long-distance communication and on ritual occasions.

The log drum is a hollow idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.243. It is mostly made of wood or bamboo, hollowed into a closed resonating chamber with one or more slits, and the slits may form tongues; the sound is made by striking the edges of the slit with a stick or a soft beater. It is found in Africa, Southeast Asia and Oceania, and also in the Americas. In Africa it is often set up in a river valley for long-distance communication; in Java, Indonesia, the wooden drum is used to wake people for the pre-dawn meal in Ramadan; the upright slit drums of Vanuatu, carved with spirit figures, have become a national emblem; and the wooden drums of the Wa people in China and Myanmar were once connected with rites for the mountain god and the new-rice festival.

Similar instruments in Vanuatu are made from large logs. 木槽鼓起源於非洲和太平洋地區的原住民文化。在非洲，特別是中部和西部地區，古老的部: The log drum originated in the indigenous cultures of Africa and the Pacific. In Africa, especially the central and western regions, old tribal civilisations already made percussion instruments from hollowed logs, for communication and for ritual. Similar instruments developed independently in the Pacific islands, Southeast Asia and among the native peoples of the Americas. This plain and effective design uses the resonance of natural timber to produce a deep, carrying sound.
站於琴前，雙手持棒敲擊琴鍵中央。手持樂器本體，透過敲擊、搖晃、刮奏或撥彈等方式使: Stand in front of the instrument and strike the middle of the bars with a beater in each hand. Hold the instrument itself and make it vibrate by striking, shaking, scraping or plucking. Different parts and different force give different timbres. In practising, first get the holding position right, then, once the basic way of sounding the instrument is secure, work on rhythm patterns and melody. Strike the surface with fingers or a beater and let the rebound carry the hand back naturally, keeping the wrist relaxed.
隨著全球文化交流的深入，木槽鼓逐漸傳入世界各地的音樂傳統中。現代樂團和民族音樂家: As cultural exchange around the world has deepened, the log drum has gradually entered musical traditions everywhere. Modern ensembles and folk musicians have taken the instrument up, making it an important element of world music and experimental music. From ritual instrument to contemporary stage, the log drum bears witness to a long human exploration of percussion, and its plain design holds a deep cultural content.
